# The fog signal

The diaphone runs on compressed air, and the compressor needs eleven minutes
to bring the receiver to working pressure from cold. Start it when visibility
falls below the far beacon, not when it falls below the near one, or the
signal begins late.

The blast pattern is one blast of three seconds every thirty seconds. A
pattern that drifts is worse than a silent signal, because a mariner counting
the interval against the chart will place the station somewhere it is not.

The compressor's drive belt slips once the rubber hardens with age, and the
first symptom is a blast that sounds correct but runs a half second short.
Time the blast with a watch whenever the air pressure gauge looks normal and
the sound does not.
